 JUDGMENT This petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act 1989 against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that: That on 26.10.2022 at about 01.00 p.m, the petitioner was riding the Motor Cycle bearing No. KA55V4584 in extreme left side, when he reached at TN Pura Kollegal Main Road, near Kuruburu Gate, TN Pura Taluk, Mysore District, at that time, suddenly the driver of Bolero Pickup bearing No.TN28AZ3822 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's Motor Cycle.

Due to which the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and was immediately shifted to Nirmala Multi Speciality hospital, Mysore, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 26.10.2022 to 27.10.2022 and later was shifted to KIMS hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 27.10.2022 to 03.11.2022 and he is still continuing the followup treatment and has spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges and prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy and was aged about 66 years and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m in his livelihood by working as Coolie.

Due to accidental injuries till today cannot attend to his work properly, which resulted in loss of earning capacity and loss of income and put to great hardship and he was completely bedridden and undergoing deep mental shock, pain and sufferings and permanent disabled.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending Bolero Pickup vehicle involved in the accident and in this regard the T.Narasipura Police have registered a case against driver of the said offending Bolero Pickup vehicle.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the insurer and the respondent No.2 being the RC Owner of the said offending Bolero Pickup vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ with interest and costs.
03. On service of summons, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of summons, the respondent No.2 did not appeared before the tribunal and hence, was placed exparte.

04. The respondent No.1 in its written statement denied the entire case of the petitioner, alleged accident, negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner, medical expenses, age, avocation, income of the petitioner and contended that the rider of the Motor Cycle rode the same without driving licence, without competence to ride the Motor Cycle, rode in rash and negligent manner, hit the insured vehicle Bolero Pickup bearing No.TN28AZ3822 and caused accident and said Bolero Pickup bearing No.TN28AZ3822 was insured with this respondent under the Policy No.AVO/2374/10319045 valid from 21.09.2022 to 20.09.2023.

The liability of this respondent, if any, is subject to terms and conditions of the policy Prabhuswamy .L vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167041738/
2 and provisions of M.V. Act and also denied that the respondent No.2 is the owner of the Bolero Pickup bearing No.TN28AZ3822 at the time of accident and the compensation claimed is highly excessive and hence, pray to dismiss the petition against respondent No.1.
05.

sentences.text: Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by my learned predecessor:  ISSUES 01.
Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 26.10.2022, at about 01.00. p.m, on T.N. Pura, Kollegala Main Road, near Kuruburu Gate.

T. N.
Pura Taluk, Mysuru, due to rash and negligent act of driving of the Jeep bearing registration No.TN28AZ3822 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
02.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
03. What Order or Award?

06. In order to prove his case, petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and the doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability is examined as PW.2 and got marked 14 documents as Ex.P.1 to 14 and closed their side evidence.
Despite sufficient opportunity has been given, the respondent No.1 did not lead evidence, hence, respondent No.1 evidence is taken as nil.
07. I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.1 and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as under: Issue No.1 In the Affirmative Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 As per final order for the following:
REASONS 09. Issue No.1: The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chiefexamination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

Though he has been elaborately crossexamined by the respondent No.1 counsel, but nothing is elicited from his mouth to disbelieve the case of the petitioner and denied that this accident occurred due to his negligence and also stated that the complaint was lodged after 4 days of accident as he was admitted in the hospital.

10. Further, the PW.2 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner sustained fracture of right rib 1 to 7, comminuted undisplaced fracture body of left scapula and he assessed permanent physical disability of 20% of right upper limb which is 7% to the whole body and has produced OPD book and Xray as per Ex.P.13 and 14.
11.
Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 14 documents as Ex.
P.1 to 14
on his behalf

. Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the T.Narasipura Police against the driver of the offending Prabhuswamy .L vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167041738/
3 Bolero Pickup vehicle.

sentences.text: Ex.P.2 is a copy of Complaint lodged against driver of the offending vehicle for his rash and negligent driving of Bolero Pickup vehicle which was caused the accident.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Sketch which indicates that there was a negligence on the part of the offending vehicle driver.

Ex.P.5 is Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against driver of offending Bolero Pickup vehicle and the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle and causing grievous injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.6 is copy of IMV report indicates that the involvement of both vehicles in the accident.
Ex.P.7 is copy of Wound certificate of the petitioner which indicates that petitioner has sustained injuries, upon which injury No.2 is grievous in nature.
Ex.P.8 is copy of Aadhaar card of the petitioner.
Ex.P.9 and 10 are Discharge summaries which shows that petitioner was taken treatment as inpatient nearly for 10 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.13 is OPD book and Ex.P.14 is Xray.

12. On going through the oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioner, the petitioner has established and proved that the he sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 26.10.2022 at about 01.00 p.m, near Kuruburu Gate, TN Pura Taluk, Mysore District, due to rash and negligent act of driving of Bolero Pickup bearing No.TN28AZ3822 by its driver as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was aged about 66 years and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m by working as Coolie and has incurred Rs.2,00,000/ towards medical,
conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges and due to accidental injuries, he became permanent disablement and suffering loss of income.
14.

It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card to show his exact date of birth and he has not produced any evidence regarding his avocation and income.
But he has produced Ex.P.8 Aadhaar card, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.1956 and the alleged accident occurred on 26.10.2022.
Eventhough the said document is taken into consideration, it appears that as on the date of accident the petitioner was aged about 66 years and the same is considered for calculating compensation.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 66 and above is 5 and the same is considered.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors.

sentences.text: 15. As stated above with regard to avocation and income the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.

Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the LokAdalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2022 to be taken as Rs.15,500/ p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the petitioner is at Rs.15,500/.
16.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner has sustained fracture of right rib 1 to 7,
Prabhuswamy .L vs Universal Sampo Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167041738/
4 comminuted undisplaced fracture body of left scapula and he assessed permanent physical disability of 20% of right upper limb which is 7% to the whole body.
Hence, considering the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 7%.

Therefore,
the loss of future income works out as under;
15,500/ x 12 x 5 x 7% = Rs.65,100/.
17.
Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.9 and 10 Discharge summaries, according to which the petitioner was admitted to Nirmala Multi Speciality hospital and KIMS hospital as inpatient for 10 days.

During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charge, special diet,
transportation and nutrition.
Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/ under this head.
18. Pain and sufferings:

As per Ex.P.7 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor and Ex.P.13 OPD book and Ex.P.14 Xray and on account of accidental injuries petitioner would have undergone pain and agony and he has sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered by him in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/ under this head.
19. Loss of income during laid up period:

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.15,500/ p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for 10 days as inpatient.
Considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 2 months.

Thus, taking into account the notional income of the petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.31,000/
(Rs.15,500 x 2) under this head.
20. Medical expenses: As per Ex.P.12 the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.52,830/.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.52,830/ under the head of medical expenses.
21. Loss of future amenities in life and unhappiness:

Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and the disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness,
the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
22. Future medical expenses:

The PW.2 in his evidence has not stated anything about future medical expenses of the petitioner and also stated that the radiological examination shows fractures are united and no evidence on record to show that petitioner require future surgery and future treatment.
Therefore, under this head the petitioner is not entitled for any compensation.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below: Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No. in Rs.
1. Loss of future income 65,10000
2. Pain and Sufferings 30,00000 3.
Attendant charges, extra 30,00000 nutritious food and conveyance charges 4.
Medical Expenses 52,83000 5. Loss of future amenities in 30,00000 life and unhappiness 6. Loss of income during laid 31,00000 up period
Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,38,930/ with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
25. Though the respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal and filed written statement, but not lead any evidence.

The respondent No.1 in its written statement admits that the insurance policy of the offending Bolero Pickup vehicle is valid from 21.09.2022 to 20.09.2023 and the alleged accident was occurred on 26.10.2022.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the insurance policy of the offending Bolero Pickup vehicle is valid and is in force.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending Bolero Pickup vehicle and respondent No.2 being the RC Owner of the offending Bolero Pickup vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount with interest from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
26. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,38,930/ (Rupees Two lakhs thirty eight thousand nine hundred and thirty only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.1 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.

Since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount with accrued interest shall be released in favour of petitioner through Epayment directly to his account by obtaining the bank account details.
